name: Night sky guide
description: A stargazing newsletter: the moon’s phases and Saturn drawn with table cells, Milky Way and Andromeda photos, a sky calendar and a star-party RSVP.

settings.title: Your sky this month: Saturn, a full moon and Andromeda 🔭
settings.previewText: What to look for, when to look up, and a star party at Jabi Lake. Issue 27 of the Night Sky Club.

children.name: Stars
Text
children.content: The longest nights of the year are coming, and the sky is putting on a show. Here’s what to find, and when.

children.name: Image
children.alt: The Milky Way rising over dark mountains, the horizon glowing pink

children.name: Moon phases
Text
children.content: New moon in week one gives the darkest skies of the month – the best time for the Milky Way. Full moon arrives in week four.

children.name: Saturn
Text
children.content: High in the south after sunset, steady and golden. Any small telescope shows the rings – ours will be pointed at it all evening.

children.name: Text
children.content: No moon after 9pm. Find the Milky Way low in the south-west.

children.name: Text
children.content: A crescent moon sits just below the ringed planet at dusk.

children.name: Text
children.content: Bright enough to read by. Look for the dark “seas” with your eyes alone.

children.name: Image
children.alt: The Andromeda galaxy, a glowing spiral among stars

children.name: Text
children.content: Andromeda, 2.5 million light years away – the farthest thing you can see without a telescope. On a dark night it’s a faint smudge north-east of the Great Square.

children.name: Text
children.content: Eight telescopes, hot chocolate and a guided tour of the sky. Free for members; bring a friend.
